name: Let Us Brew an AI Model — release manifest
description: Canonical single release record: tag, tag-target commit, PDF build commit, PDF sha256, and the SHA-256 of ALL SEVEN tokenizer files under artifacts/tokenizer/. Asserted by scripts/verify_release.py (phase D) against git, the built PDF, and the files on disk — including a check that the pin list below is exactly the set of tokenizer files the book cites, so an unpinned tokenizer cannot pass the gate. The tokenizer hashes are the SHA-256 of each tokenizer FILE ON DISK (the reproducible identifier the book cites); run manifests additionally record each tokenizer's in-memory vocabulary hash, which is a different quantity.

reproduction_from_a_clean_clone.structure: Two commits, two roles. The tag v20261001 (tag_target_commit a45a881158ed076f615f6d3bc2e72640dc5cdced) is the experiment-data snapshot whose manifests and manuscript state the book's numbers cite; the scored dataset files are gitignored and ship in no commit — they are NOT regenerable from the shipped generator at HEAD, because src/data_generator/generator.py drifted after they were generated (see the datasets block below, which records each file's producing commit and producing script). The release gate (scripts/verify_release.py) and the corrected run scripts live at the PDF build commit (this file's pdf_build_commit field) and later — the tag predates the verifier, so a checkout of the tag alone CANNOT run the release gate.
reproduction_from_a_clean_clone.build_commit_provenance: the recorded pdf_build_commit is the commit the PDF was built from; check it out only to inspect that exact source state — the verification commands below run at HEAD.
run_the_release_gate: git checkout HEAD   # the gate and pins live at HEAD; the build commit is recorded for provenance, and the gate asserts the PDF content matches it

python3.11 -m venv .venv-311 && .venv-311/bin/pip install --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu -r requirements-lock.txt && .venv-311/bin/pip install -e . && .venv-311/bin/pip install pytest

pdf.note: tracked in git (the book/*.pdf ignore rule is negated for this one path), so the sha256/page_count pins are verifiable from a clean clone — same policy as the EPUB (R2-EX-N06).

epub.note: This pin verifies the SHIPPED artifact, not a rebuild: the EPUB was built 2026-11-08 with no SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, so pandoc stamped dcterms:modified (2026-11-08T01:01:13Z) and every zip entry mtime with the wall-clock build time and minted a fresh urn:uuid (f5ff5397-617f-4c81-8a75-463fa7cb8a9a, mirrored in toc.ncx) — a rebuild of the same sources therefore produced different bytes and could never match this sha256. book/build_epub.py now pins both (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1789084800 -> 2026-09-11T00:00:00Z, and --metadata identifier=urn:uuid:f5ff5397-617f-4c81-8a75-463fa7cb8a9a), verified by building twice into a scratch location and comparing sha256 (byte-identical). Rebuilds are now reproducible relative to each other, but they still differ from THIS pin until the EPUB is rebuilt and re-pinned. Round-3 MIMO-R3-EX-03.

datasets.produced_by_commit_derivation: git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- <path> returns nothing for every file here (artifacts/datasets/ is gitignored and ships in no commit), so the fallback git log -1 was taken on the PRODUCING SCRIPT: git log -1 --format=%H -- scripts/generate_data.py = e753eff7 (the commit that added the generator entry point; unchanged since) and git log -1 --format=%H -- scripts/make_human_test.py = eaf6e14. Both predate the generator drift in 15406031, and regenerating from an archive of e753eff7 reproduces all four generate_data.py pins byte-for-byte — that is what makes 'check out the producing commit to regenerate' true rather than aspirational.

files.note: gitignored; hash pins the content the book's numbers were scored on. Produced at eaf6e14 by scripts/make_human_test.py — NOT by scripts/generate_data.py.
